clues.kinetics: It is extensively bound to serum proteins and is primarily metabolized by CYP2C9 in the liver, with most of the drug excreted in bile as inactive metabolites.
clues.substance: The active moiety has a molecular weight of 252.27, and the label names no salt form.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as a 125 mg per 5 mL oral suspension, with recommended doses of 300 mg/day.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated after prior acute hepatotoxicity and with delavirdine, and a morbilliform rash is the most common adverse reaction.
clues.indication: Tonic-clonic (grand mal) and psychomotor (temporal lobe) seizures.
clues.mechanism: Thought to block voltage-dependent membrane sodium channels, reducing sustained high-frequency neuronal discharges.

tell: An anticonvulsant whose liver enzymes saturate at high levels, so a 10% dose rise can push serum levels up disproportionately.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: peak levels occur 1½ to 3 hours after administration
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The plasma half-life in man after oral administration of phenytoin averages 22 hours
